newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish CPI to fall to 1.7 pct in May - BoA.
newsitem.headline: Spanish CPI to fall to 1.7 pct in May - BoA.

text.p: Bank of America in Madrid said on Monday it had revised downward its forecasts for Spain's 1997 consumer price index, saying it expected inflation to hit bottom at 1.7 percent in May.
In a note to clients, the bank said its revised forecasts look for a 2.2 percent rate year-on-year by year end.
That compares with a previous forecast of 2.5 percent.
"We revised down our forecasts mainly because of the fast rate with which inflation is improving," said Henrik Lumholdt, chief economist at Bank of America in Madrid.
In March, Spanish CPI rose at an yearly rate of 2.2 percent, down from 2.5 percent in February and from 2.9 percent in January.
A week ago, Spanish Economy Secretary Cristobal Montoro said inflation could dip below two percent in the next two months.
"After May we expect CPI to pick up because of an unfavourable comparison with the year-ago period, but especially because of a likely consumption recovery," Lumholdt said.

This expected decline in inflation "would leave ample room for further monetary easing by the Bank of Spain. But we think it will follow a cautious strategy because it has to eye the peseta's performance and financial markets conditions prior to undertaking further rate cuts", the note to clients added.
